What is tTJSVariant

　The tTJSVariant type is a type for handling "variable" data in TJS2.
The tTJSVariant type has an internal type, and a single type can represent void (undefined), objects, integers, real numbers, strings, and octet sequences.
Also, regarding operations, conversions between these internal types are handled automatically.

tTJSVariantType

An enumeration type representing the internal type of tTJSVariant. It can be retrieved using the tTJSVariant::Type method.

tvtVoid
　void type. This becomes the type when a tTJSVariant type is constructed with a no-argument constructor. It is not null.
tvtObject
　Object type. This is the internal type when it is null.
tvtString
　String type.
tvtOctet
　Octet sequence type.
tvtInteger
　Integer type. Holds a numeric value of type tTVInteger.
tvtReal
　Real number type. Holds a numeric value of type tTVReal.

Object Reference

Among internal types, objects are managed using a reference counting method.
tTJSVariant itself manages reference counting automatically, but please note that it does not manage reference counting after a pointer to an object is extracted from methods that retrieve the iTJSDispatch2 interface or methods that retrieve the tTJSVariantClosure type from tTJSVariant.

Object Type

The tTJSVariantClosure type is a type that holds an object inside tTJSVariant. This type has a mechanism to hold two iTJSDispatch2 interfaces: one is the object itself, and the other holds information about the context in which the object is executed.
The tTJSVariantClosure type has each method that the iTJSDispatch2 interface has. Accessing these methods via tTJSVariantClosure allows you to handle the execution context correctly.

To extract the tTJSVariantClosure type from the tTJSVariant type, there are two methods: tTJSVariant::AsObjectClosure and tTJSVariant::AsObjectClosureNoAddRef. The former increments the object's reference counter, while the latter does not.
Since the tTJSVariantClosure type does not have a mechanism to automatically manage the reference counter, care must be taken regarding reference counter management after extracting the tTJSVariantClosure type from the tTJSVariant type.

String Type

Strings in TJS2 are managed using reference counting; simple copying only increments the string's reference counter without duplicating the string body itself.
The tTJSVariantString type is a type for managing strings used in the tTJSVariant type and the tTJSString type. To extract the tTJSVariantString type from the tTJSVariant type, you can use tTJSVariant::AsString (this method increments the reference counter). However, because the tTJSVariantString type itself does not have a mechanism to automatically manage the reference counter, caution is required when using tTJSVariantString.
Since the tTJSString type can manage the reference counter, converting to the tTJSString type will be easier (conversion operators between tTJSVariant and tTJSString are defined).

Octet Sequence Type

Octet sequences in TJS2 are also managed using reference counting, just like the string type.
The tTJSVariantOctet type is a type for managing octet sequences. Please note that this type, like tTJSVariantString and tTJSVariantClosure, does not have a mechanism to manage the reference counter. To extract the tTJSVariantOctet type from the tTJSVariant type, you can use tTJSVariant::AsOctet (which increments the reference counter) or tTJSVariant::AsOctetNoAddRef (which does not increment the reference counter).

Conversion

Since various conversion operators and constructors are defined for tTJSVariant, it can be handled like a primitive type.
As mentioned above, sufficient care must be taken when performing conversions with types managed by reference counting.

Operations

Since various operators are overloaded, operations can also be performed similarly to primitive types. Type conversions required during operations are handled automatically.
